properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 22 at 4:03AM EDT until October 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and
low lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow
flooding. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 22 at 4:03AM EDT until October 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, up to 2 to 4 ft of
inundation above ground level in low- lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents and large
breaking waves expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Flooding will
extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and
businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles will
be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep
even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first
into the bottom causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...NC-12 between the Basnight Bridge and
Rodanthe remains closed. Significant ocean overwash impacts are
expected to continue for vulnerable oceanside areas today,
especially around high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Western Beaver County in southern Utah...

Milford, moving northeast at 30 mph.

roofs, siding, and trees.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Big Rock burn scar and Ohio burn
scar.

* WHERE...Portions of central and southeast Idaho, including the
following areas, in central Idaho, Wood River Foothills. In
southeast Idaho, Upper Snake River Plain.

* WHEN...From this evening through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Big Rock and Ohio burn scar is
expected up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near
the Big Rock and Ohio burn scar should prepare for potential debris
flow. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding and debris
flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Big Rock and Ohio burn scar, which may lead to
flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Heise.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Esmeralda County in south central Nevada...

* WHEN...Until 400 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1245 AM PDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Coaldale Junction as well as portions of Highway 6, Highway 95,
Fish Lake Valley Road, and Silver Peak Road.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 12:21AM MST until October 22 at 8:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Apache County in northeastern Arizona...

* Until 915 AM MDT Thursday.

* At 121 AM MDT, a river gauge on Chine Creek within Canyon de Chelly
National Monument reported a rapid rise above flood stage from
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Flash
flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Chine Creek.

* For Chinle Creek at Chinle:
At 1:00am the stage was 4.1 feet.
Flood Stage is 4.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 3.6 feet: Chinle Creek becomes impassable to recreational
vehicles.
At 4.0 feet: Water begins to encroach upon structures just upstream
of the Highway 64 bridge near the Canyon de Chelly welcome center.
At 4.3 feet: Flooding to homes and residences in Chinle on left
bank downstream from Highway 64 bridge.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chinle, Canyon De Chelly National Monument and Mummy Cave Overlook.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Junction Overlook, White House Overlook, Antelope House Overlook and
Face Rock Overlook.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Chinle Wash, Coyote Wash, Muerto, Canyon del, Sheep Dip Creek,
Black Rock Canyon and Nazlini Wash.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 12:11AM PDT until October 22 at 2:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
At 1211 AM PDT, Doppler radar indicated most showers and
thunderstorms have moved to the north and east of the warned area.
However, flash flooding will likely continue for at least the next
few hours. Additional showers along with rock slides and mud slides
are possible.



HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by showers and thunderstorms. Rock
slides and mud slides.

SOURCE...Radar and Gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas. Rock slides and mud slides.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Santa Barbara, Montecito, Carpinteria, Summerland, Goleta, Mission
Canyon, Hope Ranch, Old Man Mountain and Highway 154 over San Marcos
Pass.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Water can rise rapidly in hilly terrain and in urban areas.

Rock slides and mud slides are likely, especially around mountain and
foothill roadways.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 22 at 2:00AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon and
Friday afternoon. Relative humidity values are forecast to drop
into the 25 to 35 percent range. The 20 ft wind forecast is at or
less than 10 mph, which will limit critical fire weather
conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that may
ignite.

Numerous local burn bans remain in place across LA and MS due to
ongoing drought conditions. This includes East Feliciana, St.
Helena, Tangipahoa, and Washington Parishes along with Wilkinson,
Amite, Pike, and now Walthall Counties. Regardless, outdoor
burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and all local
restrictions followed.

Additional statements, Fire Weather Watches or Red Flag Warnings
will be possible in the upcoming days as drought conditions
worsen, relative humidity values remain low during the afternoon,
and eventually winds begin to increase, especially this weekend.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS TODAY AND INTO THE WEEKEND

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 21 at 11:49PM PDT until October 22 at 1:45AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central Inyo County in south central California...

* WHEN...Until 145 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1149 PM PDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Up to 0.5 inches
of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Panamint Springs and Homewood Canyon-Valley Wells.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 2:38AM EDT until October 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...New Kent, Gloucester, Eastern King William, Eastern
King and Queen and York Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow flooding is expected in the most vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Expect up to one foot of water
above ground level in low lying, vulnerable areas. Some roads
and low lying property including parking lots, parks and lawns
near the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.
